newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks, peso seen soft on Brazil woes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks, peso seen soft on Brazil woes.

text.p: Traders saw stocks opening with downside potential on Wednesday amid cautious dealing with players closely watching developments after Tuesday's plunge on the Brazilian equity markets.
"We withstood Brazil quite well yesterday, but there was a lot of fallout so we'll wait and see," a desk trader said.
Technical analysts placed support for the IPC index at 4,660 points, down from Tuesday's close of 4,694.35.
Peso traders said they would also keep a close eye on the Brazilian equity markets to see whether that would trigger a repeat of Tuesday's speculative run on the peso.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.9100/7.9600 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9300/7.9425 per dollar, compared to Tuesday's close of 7.9150/7.9250.

Overnight rates on Cetes were expected to open up from a prior close of 21.00 percent under pressure from a weaker peso and to line up with primary rate increases at Tuesday night's central bank auction.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 19.25 percent, a rise of 88 basis points since last week's auction.
This compares with an average predicted rise of 99 basis points in a previously conducted Reuters survey.
